 Three seasons, three finals—Sudurpaschim Royals do it again
 The Royals defeated Chitwan Rhinos in Qualifier 2 on Thursday to book a seat in the final for the third consecutive season. Sudurpaschim Royals players celebrate after the win over Chitwan Rhinos at the TU International Cricket Stadium in Kirtipur, Kathmandu, on Thursday.  Hemanta Shrestha/TKP bookmark facebook 
 twitter 
 Whatsapp 
 mail 
 Nayak Paudel 
 Published at : November 20, 2026 Updated at : November 20, 2026 07:49 Kirtipur Call it destiny, resilience, or sheer habit, but you simply cannot keep Sudurpaschim Royals away from a Nepal Premier League final. 
 For the third consecutive season, the tournament’s most consistent powerhouse found a way back to the title clash—proving that even when the traditional path through Qualifier 1 breaks down, their journey to the summit remains inevitable. 
 Sudurpaschim, which had finished second in the league stage, had to play Qualifier 2 after losing to Lumbini Lions on Tuesday. It was the first time in three seasons that the Royals had not finished at the top of the points table and lost Qualifier 1.  
 But it was not easy for the two-time finalists to reach the final for a record third time. The Royals had a tough battle against Chitwan Rhinos in front of a packed TU International Cricket Stadium.  
 Fresh from a massive victory over Kathmandu Gorkhas in Eliminator on Wednesday, Chitwan had won the toss and elected to bat first. The Rhinos were hoping to post another massive total, repeating the 200+ score they had posted against Kathmandu. 
 It was Kamil Mishara who smashed the record highest individual score of the NPL to post a target of 205 runs against Kathmandu. After the 61-run victory over the Gorkhas, Mishara had said that he wanted to contribute similarly against Sudurpaschim. But it was not meant to be. 
 Mishara (4 off 3) was the first wicket to fall for Chitwan, as he was caught behind in the second over, which was bowled by Scott Kuggeleijn. Then what followed were more wickets—Dev Khanal (6 off 9), Ravi Bopara (1 off 8), Bibek Yadav (3 off 11), Kushal Malla (1 off 5), Usama Mir (2 off 5), Salahuddin Khan (18 off 16), Kamal Singh Airee (10 off 8) and Rijan Dhakal (3 off 4). 
 The only reason Chitwan could post at least 133/9 by the end of the first innings was Dawid Malan. Malan, who came in at three, was the last man standing for Chitwan after Dhakal got run out in the last ball of the innings. 
 Malan, with the help of nine fours and two sixes, was not out at 71 off 51. The Rhinos, struggling with the bat, were more than happy to take 14 runs as extras, including 3 byes and 11 wides. 
 Kuggeleijn picked three wickets, Tharindu Ratnayake claimed two, and Hemant Dhami, Dipendra Singh Airee and Ishan Pandey took one each for Sudurpaschim. 
 The Royals, backed by a loud and passionate crowd, were the favourites based on the target. But the Rhinos were not in the mood of making it easier for the Royals. 
 The way the chase went for the Royals, there were many moments when the game turned towards Chitwan. 
 The Royals had lost four wickets in 10 overs, when the score stood at 58, one run fewer than what Chitwan had managed in their first 10 overs. 
 The wickets of George Munsey (8 off 15), Binod Bhandari (23 off 13), Pandey (2 off 5), Kuggeleijn (2 off 5), Airee (15 off 16), Aarif Sheikh (10 off 10) and Fabian Allen (5 off 10) had put the Royals under pressure. But until Ratnayake was on the crease, the Royals were never out of the chase. 
 Ratnayake, at 53 off 42, stayed not out for the fourth time in the season. It would not have been possible had he been caught out by Kamal Singh in the 15th over.  
 Ratnayake was at 18 when he attempted a maximum in the third ball of the 15th over, and Kamal missed it while he tried saving his head—the confusion seemed to have been due to the light. 
 Ratnayake smashed the penultimate ball of the last over for a four to complete the chase, win the match by three wickets and take the Royals to another final. 
 “I want to thank my coach for encouraging me,” Ratnayake said after bagging the player of the match award. “This is a tricky wicket and I did my basics. The plan was to take the game deep.” 
 Ratnayake was lifted in the air by his teammates after the win, as he had just taken the Royals to another final. 
 “I was under pressure at the dugout when the chase was underway,” Airee said after the win. “Tharindu played very well.” 
 Bopara, the Chitwan skipper, was not happy after the loss, but he was happy with how the team had improved over the years. 
 “I am proud of the boys,” said Bopara, the all-time leading NPL run scorer who has played in all three seasons. “It is great to see how they have improved over the three years.” 
 Meanwhile, the Royals are ready for another final and their maiden title. 
 “Win and loss is part of the game,” Airee said. “But my intuition says that the final will be a good one for us. It will be a tough competition though.” 
 Lumbini Lions will defend their title against Sudurpaschim on Saturday. It will be the consecutive season where the two teams are competing in the final. 
 Nayak Paudel 
 Nayak Paudel covers sports for The Kathmandu Post. He previously worked at the Post (2018–19) and spent over five years at The Rising Nepal. His reporting spans crime, health, education, and social issues.
